By explicitly separating sources by reliability and timeliness, it prevents contamination of high-quality Tier-1 data with low-grade Tier-5 noise. However, the rigid discretization can create artificial boundaries; when information flows continuously across scales, the hierarchy may introduce bias through forced categorization.
